Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

synthcheck 0.3.0

  • New persona_fidelity() and gg_persona_fidelity(): A check of whether the personas given to a language model change its answers. For each model and scale it compares the variance between personas (eta squared) with shuffled persona labels, and when the persona table holds target_<scale> columns, it checks that each persona’s scale scores move in the intended direction. Scores can be standardized against real data.

  • authenticity_benchmark() now gives an interval for every anchored value and for the score (*_lower, *_upper; new arguments conf and n_boot). It is a bootstrap over the model’s attempts and over the floor and ceiling draws, so two models whose intervals overlap are not clearly apart. gg_benchmark() prints the intervals under the values (intervals = TRUE), print() adds the score interval, and summarise_benchmark() says when a model’s interval overlaps with the next one’s.

  • Three short instruments with well-documented item problems, each with real responses from the Open-Source Psychometrics Project: The Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (rses_items, rses_real; a negative-wording method factor), the DASS-21 (dass_items, dass_real; a disputed three-factor structure) and the Mini-IPIP (mini_ipip_items, mini_ipip_real; poor fit and a weak Intellect/Imagination scale). The issue column of each item table says what has been reported about each item, with references in the help pages.

  • New sc_builtin_instrument() returns any bundled instrument, with its response scale, category labels and instructions.

  • The app’s Instrument tab offers all four built-in instruments, and the Compare tab’s built-in real data follow the instrument chosen there, with a country filter.

  • New article: “Short instruments with known item problems”.

  • The Designer card on the app’s About tab has the full contact details, links to the designer’s website, blog, ORCID and GitHub, and how to cite synthcheck with its Zenodo DOI. It no longer ends in a large blank space.

  • New response cache: generate_synthetic() and cognitive_interview() save every answer on disk (sc_cache()), under a key made of the provider, model, temperature, prompts, respondent, attempt, retry and seed. The same run again reads the answers back: It is repeatable and costs nothing. More attempts or respondents call the models only for the new ones. mode = "refresh" asks again, cache = FALSE turns it off, and sc_cache_info() and sc_cache_clear() show and delete what is saved. Failed calls and mock answers are never saved.

  • New estimate_cost() and estimate_interview_cost(): What a run is likely to cost before it starts, from the number of calls, guessed tokens and a price table (sc_prices, with the date of each price). Ollama models and cached calls are free. You can pass your own prices.

  • The app shows the estimated cost under the run plan of the Models and Interviews tabs and asks you to confirm before a run with paid models. A new setting chooses whether to reuse, refresh or skip saved answers, and a button clears the cache.

  • With one respondent per call, a retry now asks only for the items still missing, in both the one-at-a-time and the parallel paths.

  • New write_report() writes the results as one report: A self-contained HTML file (the default) or a PDF, with the plots, tables, plain-language summaries and the settings needed to repeat the run. It covers the benchmark, the pretest and the cognitive interviews, and keeps the caveat that the benchmark does not show that synthetic data can replace a field test. The PDF uses the PDF device that comes with R, so it needs no LaTeX or pandoc.

  • The app’s Export tab has a new Results report card that downloads the report for the path you chose, in HTML or PDF.

  • New article: “Getting an API key for OpenAI or Claude”. It walks through signing up, adding credit, keeping the key private and setting a spending limit. The app’s Models tab links to it and to the providers’ sign-up pages next to the API key fields, and the website links to it from the app menu, Get started and the README.

  • The guided tour in the app now shows the API keys, the estimated cost and the response cache. The About tab lists the cost estimate and the cache.

  • The tour of the app, the app demos, Get started and the tutorial on generating respondents cover the built-in short instruments, the cost estimate, the response cache and the results report, with new screenshots.

synthcheck 0.2.0

Adds a path for scales without real data (a synthetic pretest and cognitive interviews with language models), a redesigned app and updated documentation.

  • New synthetic_pretest() for scales without real data: Pilot screening of the items on synthetic respondents alone (item-rest correlations, alpha if an item is dropped, items that barely vary or duplicate another item, reverse keys, GRM slopes with mirt, alpha and parallel analysis per scale). It checks whether the flags hold across models, temperatures, prompt wordings or persona sets (by), in every attempt, and whether the designed structure (the scale and reverse columns) comes back. gg_pretest() draws the flagged items and the scales, and summarise_pretest() describes the result in plain language. It is screening, not validation.

  • The app now asks first whether you have real data. With real data, the fourth tab is Compare (the benchmark); without it, the fourth tab is the new Pretest tab. The Models tab can add one model at several temperatures for the stability check, and Export saves the pretest and its R script.

  • New article: “Pretesting a scale without real data”.

  • New cognitive interviews for items without real data: cognitive_interview() has language models play each persona, think aloud while answering an item and answer scripted verbal probes (sc_probes(), after Willis, 2005), then a separate call codes each transcript for comprehension, retrieval, judgement, response-mapping and sensitivity problems. A synthetic pretest result can choose the items and adds a probe aimed at each flag. summarise_interviews() rolls the codes up per item, flags items by fixed rules and says how they agree with the pretest, and gg_interview() draws one heatmap. sc_interview_prompts() shows what is sent. The new article “Cognitive interviews with language models” walks through it. It is a screening aid, not a substitute for cognitive interviews with real people.

  • The app has a new Interviews tab (5) on the path without real data, so Export is tab 6 there and tab 5 with real data. It runs cognitive_interview() with the personas and models of tabs 2 and 3, on the items the pretest flagged or on items you choose (the pretest is optional), with editable probes, a choice of coder, a progress bar and a Stop button. It shows the summary, the heatmap and the transcripts, and Export saves the interviews, the transcripts and the plot.

  • The app’s guided tour follows the path chosen in the first step and now covers every tab on both paths, including the designed structure on the Pretest tab and the interview settings and transcripts. The tour of the app, the app demos (with a new demo of the path without real data), Get started, the README and the help page of run_synthcheck_app() describe the final design.

  • The app has a new look in the logo colours, with the logo in the navbar and a coverage strip under it. A new About tab opens the app: It explains the purpose, lists what the app can do and produce, shows an animated picture of a language model answering survey items, gives the designer’s contact details and starts a guided tour of the five tabs (with the cicerone package, in Suggests).

  • The website matches the app: A navy navbar with the coverage strip under it, navy headings and framed screenshots. The app articles describe the About tab and the guided tour.

  • The README, citation("synthcheck") and CITATION.cff give the Zenodo DOI that covers all versions (10.5281/zenodo.24173113).

  • Figure captions on the website are italic and muted, so they read apart from the text.

  • synthcheck is no longer labelled experimental in the README, the help pages, the articles, the printed results or the app. The caveat stays: The benchmark compares models and supports decisions about them, and it does not show that synthetic data can replace a field test.

synthcheck 0.1.0

First release, archived on Zenodo. The benchmark compares models and supports decisions about them. It does not show that synthetic respondents can replace a field test.

The synthetic authenticity benchmark

  • authenticity_benchmark() builds the synthetic authenticity benchmark: Overlap, Structure and Behaviour for every model, each anchored between shuffled real columns (0) and a second sample of real people (100), with the weakest column as the default score. gg_benchmark() draws it on a scale from red (-100 or less) through pale (0) to blue (100), so values below the shuffled baseline stay readable.
  • summarise_benchmark() describes each model’s benchmark result in a few plain sentences.
  • flag_careless() flags careless real respondents, and clean_real = TRUE compares against the remaining ones.

Overlap, Structure and Behaviour

  • synthetic_coverage(), blend_llms() and gg_coverage() give Overlap, Structure and the best blend of models, drawn as a coverage strip, with theme_synthcheck(). They are ported from mirtverse.
  • behaviour_features() gives eight behaviour features per respondent (variability, extreme and midpoint answers, acquiescence, key inconsistency, even-odd consistency, Mahalanobis distance and person fit lz), synthetic_behaviour() turns them into the Behaviour index, and gg_behaviour() draws the behaviour strip.

Diagnostics beside the benchmark

These do not change the benchmark score.

  • synthetic_construct() and gg_construct() check the construct structure of each model: The gap between the synthetic and the real correlations between scales, alpha per scale (above the real value means too coherent) and Tucker’s congruence of the loadings, read against a permutation null (after Lukauskas & Šarkauskaitė, 2026).
  • respondent_coverage() and gg_respondent_coverage() give the respondent coverage gap (RCG) and the off-support ratio (OSR) of Kumagae and Kaneko (2026): Whether every real person has a synthetic look-alike, and whether synthetic respondents sit outside the real data.
  • synthetic_copula() draws respondents from a Gaussian copula of the real data, and authenticity_benchmark(copula = TRUE) adds it as a reference row.

Generating synthetic respondents

  • run_synthcheck_app() opens a Shiny app that generates synthetic respondents with several language models and benchmarks them in five tabs: Instrument, Personas, Models (API keys, temperature, attempts, a progress bar with the time left), Compare (the benchmark with a plain-language summary per model) and Export. API keys stay in memory for the session. The Instrument and Personas tabs offer CSV templates to fill in.
  • sc_instrument(), sc_personas(), sc_persona_grid(), sc_model() and sc_prompt() define what synthetic respondents take and who they are, and generate_synthetic() asks Anthropic, OpenAI or local Ollama models (through ellmer) to answer, one respondent per call.
  • write_synthetic() and read_synthetic() save and load generated data as CSV, JSON, RDS or Excel, and as_synthetic_list() turns a long table into the input of authenticity_benchmark().

Data

  • hexaco_real holds 17,874 real respondents from Canada, Great Britain and the United States, and hexaco_items the 240 IPIP-HEXACO items (both from mirtverse).
  • hexaco_llm holds 89,597 synthetic respondents from six language models, including Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-4.1 mini.

Documentation

  • The website has a Get started article, four tutorials (Overlap and Structure, Behaviour, the benchmark, generating synthetic respondents in R), an article on the diagnostics beside the benchmark, a tour of the app with screenshots of each tab, and three app demos (the built-in models, a practice run with the mock provider, and your own questionnaire).
  • citation("synthcheck"), CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json give the citation and the Zenodo metadata.
